summary:
We developed BREATHE (Earth Information Jukebox) for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: an interactive web application and scientific API that translates NASA atmospheric observations into synchronized visuals and real-time sound. Built with Next.js, TypeScript, and the Web Audio API alongside a Python, FastAPI, NumPy, and Pandas backend, BREATHE converts verified NASA GEOS-CF v2 datasets (PM2.5, PM10, CO, NO2, O3, and SO2) into playable acoustic compositions across interactive maps, rasters, and Explore, Studio, Gallery, and Learn workflows.

BREATHE addresses The Earth Information Jukebox challenge by turning complex spatiotemporal Earth data into an intuitive listening experience. Users select global grids, custom bounding regions, or A/B comparisons across UTC timestamps to hear pollutant levels, spatial contrast, and temporal change mapped to pitch, harmonics, rhythm, and multi-stem mixes, while enforcing checksum provenance and separating surface concentrations, column AOD, and AQI.

This matters because static charts can mask subtle atmospheric shifts and exclude visually impaired audiences. Pairing verified NASA science with sound makes atmospheric dynamics immediately perceptible, comparable, and memorable for researchers, educators, and the public.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

BREATHE (Earth Information Jukebox) is an interactive web platform and scientific API built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 that turns global atmospheric observations into synchronized visuals and real-time audio sonification.

  • Scientific Data Pipeline: A Python/FastAPI backend retrieves and ingests NASA GMAO GEOS-CF v2 hourly global atmospheric composition datasets (0.25°, 1440×721 NetCDF4 granules via NASA NCCS/OPeNDAP) covering six surface pollutants: PM2.5, PM10, CO, NO2, O3, and SO2. Raw data is unit-normalized, validated against :30 UTC timestamps and SHA-256 checksums, and aggregated on demand using cosine-latitude-weighted means, unweighted native-sample quantiles (P90, IQR), coverage, and spatial/temporal derivatives. Compact little-endian binary feature arrays (float32-le base64) preserve missing NaN values without turning gaps into zeros.
    • Explore: Navigate a 3D globe or flat map, inspect atmospheric layers over UTC timelines, draw custom bounding boxes or territories/polygons, and launch verified global, single-region, or side-by-side A/B comparison playback sessions.
    • Studio: Act as an atmospheric sound designer—mix four live audio stems (Field / mean, Highlights / P90 excess, Spread / IQR, and Edges / spatial derivatives), adjust key, waveform, tempo, density, brightness, spatial spread, and band selection while watching real-time waveforms, spectrograms, particle fields, and rhythm grids, then export reproducible session recipes as JSON.
    • Gallery: Browse, search, filter, bookmark, and replay curated and user-saved atmospheric soundscapes.
    • Learn: Explore guided region comparisons (such as city baselines and GEOS-CF v2 observations) that explain both the atmospheric science and how physical quantities translate into sound.
  • Real-Time Browser Synthesis: Instead of pre-rendering static audio files, BREATHE runs a custom Web Audio API AudioWorklet DSP synthesizer in the browser, locking the audio playback clock to rendered EPSG:4326 scientific raster frames so visuals and sound stay tightly synchronized during play, pause, seek, reverse playback, and buffering.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Multi-Sensory Scientific Comprehension: Visual color maps can flatten subtle gradients or hide fast-moving spikes. Mapping concentration, peak excess, spatial dispersion, and gradients to pitch, harmonic complexity, timbre, and rhythm lets users hear hotspots, diurnal cycles, and regional contrasts immediately.
  • Accessibility & Inclusion: Auditory exploration opens NASA Earth observation data to blind and low-vision users as well as learners who absorb patterns better through sound than through dense tables or charts.
  • Scientific Literacy Without Misinformation: BREATHE enforces explicit provenance badges distinguishing offline/mock datasets from verified NASA observations and clearly educates users on why column Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) is distinct from surface pollutant concentrations and public-health AQI.
  • Intended Impact: Empower researchers, educators, students, storytellers, and citizens to explore Earth's atmosphere not only as numbers on a screen, but as an intuitive, memorable, and verifiable sensory experience.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Programming Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript (ES modules & Web Audio AudioWorklet), Python 3.12, CSS, SQL.
  • Frontend Stack: Next.js 14 (App Router), React 18, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL (3D globe & 2D map rendering), Recharts, TopoJSON (topojson-client, world-atlas), Lucide React, Motion, and the native HTML5 Web Audio API.
  • Backend & Scientific Computing: FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic v2, NumPy, Pandas, xarray, netCDF4, SciPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, Psycopg 3, and HTTPX.
  • Database, Infrastructure & QA: Neon Serverless PostgreSQL and SQLite, Docker & Docker Compose, GitHub Actions CI/CD, Azure Container Apps deployment configuration, pytest, Node.js contract/cross-language numeric parity test runners, ESLint, Prettier, and TypeScript (tsc).
  • Hardware: Standard developer workstations and cloud containers; end users require only a standard computer or mobile device with a modern web browser and audio output.

How the Project Is Creative

  • Atmosphere as a Musical Score: BREATHE treats geographic sweeps (west-to-east or north-to-south across 8 or 16 spatial bands) and hourly UTC evolution as multi-voice musical arrangements—translating mean background concentrations into tonal fields, extreme P90 hotspots into melodic highlights, IQR spread into acoustic dispersion, and spatial/temporal derivatives into expressive edge textures.
  • Left/Right Stereo A/B Listening: Users can compare two regions simultaneously in stereo (Region A vs. Region B panned across channels) to hear environmental disparities directly.
  • Dual Scientific & Studio Experience: Combining an authentic geospatial explorer with a full DAW-inspired Studio and Gallery bridges rigorous Earth science and creative sound design without compromising either discipline.

Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  1. Scientific Integrity & Provenance: Computing area-weighted means with cos⁡(latitude)\cos(\text{latitude})cos(latitude), calculating quantiles from raw native samples rather than coarse grid averages, preserving NaN gaps, verifying SHA-256 file integrity on frame requests, and preventing synthetic fallbacks during verified scientific sessions.
  2. Audio-Visual Sync & Browser Stability: Offloading synthesis to an AudioWorklet thread, applying smooth gain ramps to avoid clicks, isolating high-frequency clock updates from heavy map UI trees, and gating the audio horizon on rendered frames so audio freezes cleanly rather than drifting out of sync during network buffering.
  3. Payload Efficiency & Scalability: Streaming compact float32-le binary arrays with bounded resolution/element budgets (1.2M feature elements max) and stateless frame endpoints designed for scale-to-zero containers and serverless PostgreSQL.
  4. Cross-Language Accuracy & Maintainability: Decoupling frontend and backend via versioned API contracts, shared specifications, and automated Python-to-JavaScript numeric parity tests.
